top.titulo: Brent Jumps Nearly 3% as Iran Denies Any Talks With Washington
top.titulo_es: El Brent sube casi un 3 % tras la negativa de Irán a mantener conversaciones con Washington
top.resumen_es: El crudo Brent subió casi un 3 % el miércoles hasta los 93,90 $ por barril a las 11:18 h ET, más del doble de su subida del 1,4 % a las 9:27 h, ya que Irán negó que esté negociando con Washington y los analistas no veían un final a corto plazo para la guerra. El WTI subió casi un 2 % hasta los 87,98 $ y el fuelóleo, el referente del diésel en EE. UU., se disparó un 4,1 %. top.titulo: European Gas Prices Rebound on Iran War Uncertainty
top.resumen_es: European benchmark natural gas prices rebounded on Wednesday from the one-month low hit on Tuesday, as uncertainty about the Iran war returned to the energy markets following steep selloffs in recent days. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, rose by 2.7% as of 9:30 a.m. in Amsterdam on Wednesday, topping $96.85 (87 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh). top.resumen_es: Gas-fired projects secured all 5.16 gigawatts (GW) of derated capacity in Germany's first capacity auction, with more than half going to developments at existing coal sites. top.titulo: Saudi Crude Output Jumps 26% as Riyadh Reports Near Pre-War Production
top.resumen_es: Saudi Arabia told OPEC it raised crude production in October to 10.563 million barrels per day, back near pre-war levels and slightly above its OPEC quota of about 10.5 million bpd, Bloomberg columnist Javier Blas reported on Wednesday. Output rose 26% from 8.372 million bpd in September to the highest level since February, when the kingdom reported 10.882 million bpd in the last month before the Iran war disrupted Middle East supply, according to Reuters.
